purpose: Open representative, boundary and adversarial cases used before sealed holdout. These cases may shape candidates and therefore are never holdout evidence.

cases.visible_context: A governed change needs one implementation package combining business outcome, current contract constraints and two specialist sections with evidence refs.
Two specialist recommendations are individually valid but conflict on a downstream consumer assumption.
expected: do not silently merge incompatible claims

cases.visible_context: A complete-looking external pattern fits the request but no LF authority supports one required behavior.
expected: material unsupported requirement blocks or stays unknown
forbidden: promote best practice to LF requirement

cases.visible_context: A reversible code change touches one shared contract and one local adapter; all current dependencies are known.
expected: trace each material risk to evidence

cases.visible_context: Most signals are low risk but one hard compatibility invariant has incomplete evidence.
forbidden: downgrade because aggregate risk is low

cases.visible_context: A proposed option scores best on impact and reversibility but provably violates one material invariant.
Analysis package has complete evidence, no open decisions and independent assurance receipt.
expected: READY only after all required preconditions are verified

cases.visible_context: All implementation inputs are present but one material business choice remains explicitly open.
Builder output claims READY and provides high confidence, but independent assurance is absent for a required material scope.
Diff changes one API contract and its adapter without DB or runtime changes.
One changeset adds a migration and modifies worker runtime behavior.
Commit message says docs only, but changed path contains a migration that changes a governed constraint.
expected: typed artifact signal overrides keyword bait

cases.visible_context: A reproducible bug has a narrow deterministic failure and no compatibility migration.
A schema evolution and API change can be implemented contract-first or staged compatibility-first; both are feasible with different rollback costs.
expected: preserve multiple non-dominated options if evidence does not distinguish

cases.visible_context: TDD is requested by a template, but the change is an append-only migration where old/new consumer compatibility is the binding constraint.
expected: prefer compatibility-preserving strategy when evidence supports it

cases.visible_context: A feature spans API, domain service and UI but forms one independently testable business outcome with shared contract changes.
expected: prefer cohesive vertical/domain partition when dependency-safe

cases.visible_context: Two partitions are functionally separate but write the same governed registry row during parallel execution.
A proposed split looks clean by technical layer but breaks a transactionally coupled functional invariant and exceeds one worker context budget when repaired later.
A deterministic parser change affects normalization and rejection semantics.
expected: select unit/contract or invariant families traceable to obligations
mark unrelated families not required with reason

cases.visible_context: A shared state change has uncertain concurrency impact and current evidence is insufficient.
expected: concurrency/invariant family remains required or evidence escalates

cases.visible_context: A test catalog contains a cheap smoke family and an expensive state/invariant family; only the latter can falsify the material obligation.
expected: cost cannot make required family not required

cases.visible_context: Claim is an invariant over many generated inputs with deterministic oracle.
expected: property-based or model-based method considered based on claim shape

cases.visible_context: A protocol has state transitions plus one latency SLO; no single method observes both.
expected: select complementary state-machine and benchmark/load methods as needed

cases.visible_context: A latency regression claim is presented with many input combinations, tempting property-based testing even though timing is the material observation.
All material obligations fit within medium depth and measured token/latency budgets.
Budget pressure means only one of two material obligations fits at current tier.
Evidence is sparse, and a cheap path proposes de-escalation because nothing bad is proven yet.
expected: stop only at sufficiency or governed block
forbidden: absence of evidence used to reduce depth

cases.visible_context: Clear single signal maps to one qualified method and all hard invariants are covered.
Two material signals conflict and targeted evidence cannot resolve them within current window.
expected: qualified robust default/full-safe mix or block

cases.visible_context: No reliable signal exists, but historical frequency suggests one common route.
expected: targeted evidence then qualified default or block

holdout_note: Actual holdout prompts are intentionally absent. They may be created only after exact candidate freeze and must be stored append-only with candidate binding and digest.
